skill.name: ppt-editing-skill
skill.description: Guides safe editing of existing PowerPoint PPTX files through template analysis, slide mapping, XML edits, cleanup, and validated repacking.
skill.summary: Update existing PowerPoint templates while preserving PPTX structure and layout integrity.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, XML examples, and code fences. I confirmed limited operational risks where the skill instructs external tools, helper scripts, temp-file writes, and PPTX archive handling on user-provided files.

remediation.issue: External tools process user-provided PPTX files.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before command execution, quote all paths, and run conversions in an isolated working directory.

remediation.issue: Temporary output is directed to /tmp without unique-directory guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Use a per-run directory from a secure temp API and copy final outputs atomically after validation.

remediation.issue: PPTX archive handling lacks documented traversal safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Document checks that reject absolute paths, parent-directory entries, and unsafe symlinks during unpack and repack.

content.value_statement: Manual PPTX edits can break layouts, relationships, or XML. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for template-based deck updates.
actual_capabilities: Copies a user-provided PPTX into a predictable working template file.
Extracts presentation text and structure for slide planning with markitdown.
Maps source content to varied template layouts before editing begins.
Sequences slide deletion, duplication, and reordering before XML content edits.
Guides safe slide XML text replacement, bullet formatting, and smart quote handling.
Describes cleanup and validated repacking into an edited PPTX deliverable.
limitations: Requires a usable existing PPTX file or template.
References helper scripts that must be available in the runtime environment.
Needs visual QA because long replacement text can overflow slide layouts.
Does not provide a full design system for creating decks from a blank canvas.

use_cases.title: Refresh Client Proposal Decks
use_cases.description: Replace placeholder sections, reorder slides, and keep the approved template structure intact.

use_cases.title: Adapt Internal Report Templates
use_cases.description: Convert recurring content into a polished deck while preserving layout, bullets, and section hierarchy.

use_cases.title: Localize Presentation Content
use_cases.description: Update slide text and captions across an existing presentation without rebuilding the file manually.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Template Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a small deck refresh.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ppt-editing-skill to update this PPTX template with the provided content. Preserve the original file and create edited.pptx.

prompt_templates.title: Map Content to Slides
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan slide choices before editing XML.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the extracted template structure, map each content section to a varied slide layout, then summarize the planned slide order.

prompt_templates.title: Replace Placeholder Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Edit slide XML while preserving formatting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace all placeholder titles, body text, captions, and list items in the selected slides. Preserve bullets, spacing, and XML entities.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild and QA a Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with structural edits and validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Duplicate needed template slides, remove unused slides, update the XML content, clean orphaned assets, repack the deck, and verify the output.

output_examples.input: A five-slide sales template and new customer-specific proposal copy.
output_examples.output: An edited PPTX with copied source preserved, refreshed slide text, reordered sections, and a final QA note.

output_examples.input: A quarterly report template with fewer metrics than the original placeholder deck.
output_examples.output: A cleaned presentation with excess visual groups removed, consistent bullets, and no orphaned slide assets.

output_examples.input: A presentation that needs localized headings, captions, and quoted legal terms.
output_examples.output: A repacked deck with updated text, preserved smart quotes, and layout checks for text overflow.

best_practices: Complete slide deletion, duplication, and ordering before editing slide content.
Use varied template layouts so the final deck does not become text-heavy.
Run extraction and visual QA after edits to catch overflow and missing content.
anti_patterns: Do not edit the original user-provided PPTX in place.
Do not clear unused placeholders while leaving their shapes and images behind.
Do not combine multiple list items into one XML paragraph.

faq.question: Can this skill create a deck from scratch?
faq.answer: It is optimized for editing existing PowerPoint files and templates, not blank-deck design.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: The expected deliverable is an edited PPTX file, usually named edited.pptx.

faq.question: Does it preserve the original presentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow copies the user-provided file before making changes.

faq.question: Why does it edit XML directly?
faq.answer: Direct XML editing preserves PowerPoint relationships, layout details, and formatting when done carefully.

faq.question: Does it support parallel work?
faq.answer: Yes. Separate slide XML files can be edited in parallel after structural changes are complete.

faq.question: What tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references markitdown, Python zipfile behavior, and helper scripts for unpacking, adding slides, cleaning, and packing.
